character_reference.tabby:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production 2D game sprite sheet, eight-frame looping walk animation for a tiny desktop mascot in a terminal title bar.
Primary request: an adorable anime chibi orange tabby kitten walking toward the RIGHT, in clean hand-drawn Japanese animation style. Oversized rounded head, bright blue eye in side profile, tiny pink nose and inner ears, cream muzzle and belly, three clear darker ginger stripes, soft fluffy cheek tufts, short rounded paws, a curved upright tail. Bold dark warm-brown outline, flat cel shading, simple readable shapes that remain legible when reduced to 32 pixels high. Animal kitten on four legs, no clothing or props.
Layout: EXACTLY eight complete full-body sprites in an invisible regular grid of FOUR equal columns and TWO equal rows, read left to right on the top row then left to right on the bottom row. One kitten per cell, equal scale and consistent proportions throughout. Every cat faces strictly RIGHT in profile; tail to the left, face to the right. The entire tail, ears and paws fit inside each cell with generous clear margins. All grounded paws share the same baseline within each cell. Keep the head and torso aligned in every cell with only a slight natural walk bounce.
Motion: eight successive distinct evenly spaced phases of one smooth relaxed quadruped walk cycle. Alternate front and rear paws through contact, down, passing, and up positions, then the opposite stride. Clearly change leg positions between frames; gently sway tail. Frame eight loops seamlessly to frame one. This is one consistent kitten animated eight times, not eight character designs. No horizontal translation inside cells.
Backdrop: a completely flat uniform vivid chroma green (#00FF00) background, including all margins and all space between paws and tail. No green anywhere on the kitten. No ground, shadows, gradients, scenery, props, sparkles, transparency checkerboard, panels, grid lines, text, frame numbers, signatures or watermarks.

character_reference.calico: Use case: stylized-concept. Edit this anime kitten character reference. Preserve the exact pose, silhouette, proportions, bright blue eye, cute face, four legs, curled tail, bold outlines and clean cel shading. Change only its coat into a natural calico kitten: warm white fur as the base, distinct large ginger-orange and charcoal-black patches on the ears, head, back and tail; a white muzzle, belly and paws; pink nose and inner ears. Asymmetrical calico patches, not stripes. It must read distinctly from an orange tabby and an all-black tuxedo at 32 pixels high. Keep the exact solid vivid chroma green background. One complete full-body kitten facing right, centered with all ears, tail and paws visible, no text or accessories. This is the master character reference for a walking animation.

motion.prompt: Animate this exact anime kitten in a smooth, convincing quadruped WALK CYCLE, always facing RIGHT in strict side view. Locked camera and fixed body position like a treadmill animation for a game sprite. Three complete relaxed walking cycles over three seconds; constant tempo throughout. Four distinct legs articulate naturally at shoulder/hip AND elbow/knee: each paw reaches forward, touches down, stays flat at the same ground height while sweeping backward under the body, then lifts and curls forward for recovery. Near and far legs alternate; hind paw follows the forepaw on the same side. Clear passing poses with a bent lifted paw passing the planted leg. Continuous weight shifts and subtle head/body rise and fall, a gentle tail follow-through. All four paws NEVER jump off the ground together. WALK, not run, hop, glide, paddle, march or shuffle. Do not merely rotate straight stiff legs. Preserve this kitten's face, anatomy, proportions, coat pattern, bold clean outlines and flat cel shading throughout. Same framing, scale, head direction and ground baseline throughout. Whole ears, tail and all feet remain inside the image. Background stays perfectly flat solid chroma green, no shadow, floor, marks, scenery, text, camera motion or perspective rotation. End on the starting pose so the animation can loop.
